implementationBlockedBy: The ticket lacks row-level implementation evidence.

failingDirectQuestions.question: Does the whole experience feel like a real production community app for the target users, not merely an implemented workflow harness?
failingDirectQuestions.why: The review cannot claim production-grade UX while workflow/persona lifecycle evidence, direct-question evidence, or screenshot visual inspection is incomplete/failing.
failingDirectQuestions.requiredFix: Complete workflow/persona coverage, lifecycle scorecards, and remediate visual/layout failures before claiming production-grade UX.

failingDirectQuestions.question: Is the UI modern, easy to use, easy to navigate, and visually appealing for the target persona?
failingDirectQuestions.why: Visible UI/text evidence, lifecycle scorecards, and screenshot pixel/layout inspection support judging modern UI quality.

failingDirectQuestions.question: Is the overall information architecture organized around community content and real jobs-to-be-done instead of workflow lists or validation surfaces?
failingDirectQuestions.why: Failing workflow/persona lifecycle scorecards or visual blockers prevent a holistic community IA pass.
failingDirectQuestions.requiredFix: Replace incomplete workflow-card UX with lifecycle-complete domain-native community sections and rerun scorecards.

failingDirectQuestions.question: Does the visible UI avoid blocking or major overlap, clipping, crowding, default-scaffold, repeated-card, checklist-modal, and thin-content defects?
failingDirectQuestions.why: The judge cannot clear layout/content defects while row-level evidence remains incomplete, unsupported, or visually failing.
failingDirectQuestions.requiredFix: Complete screenshot-backed review rows, fix incomplete workflow lifecycles, and remediate any row-level layout/content defects.

uxReferencePatterns.label: Material navigation and information architecture
uxReferencePatterns.whatToCopy: Organize screens by user jobs and destinations; keep primary actions visible and avoid exposing implementation taxonomy.

uxReferencePatterns.label: Apple HIG navigation and content organization
uxReferencePatterns.whatToCopy: Make navigation predictable, content-centered, and appropriate for the user’s current task.

uxReferencePatterns.label: Material Design cards and lists
uxReferencePatterns.whatToCopy: Use cards/lists only as scannable containers with clear hierarchy, content, metadata, and actions. Do not use repeated cards as the whole primary workflow.

uxReferencePatterns.label: Flutter sample app implementation patterns
uxReferencePatterns.whatToCopy: Copy the separation between app shell, route state, domain widgets, and testable UI states rather than hardcoding a single generic renderer.
